subject: Convert to annual invoice with milepost credits - ACME Health
messages:
From: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@acmehealth.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.io
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Switching ACME billing to annual invoice - initial ask

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team was impressed with the inference latency and the dashboard visibility. Procurement here is evaluating moving several ML workloads onto Redwood, but our controller requires annual invoicing for SaaS line items.

Can you share what options you have for switching from monthly/quarterly billing to an annual prepay or annual invoiced commitment? Specifically:
- What multi-year discount tiers do you offer?
- Do you provide step/milepost credits for first-year ramp?
- How do you handle true-ups if our usage grows mid-year?

We have an initial budgeted spend of roughly $480k ARR in year 1 with expected 70% growth into year 2, but we'd like flexibility on ramp and true-up cadence.

If you can send a short term sheet and any procurement-facing language we can share with our finance team that would be great.

Cheers,
Emma Shaw
Head of Data Platforms
ACME Health

P.S. SOC 2 + data residency notes would be helpful in the contract appendix.
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching ACME billing to annual invoice - initial ask

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the context. Happy to walk through options. TL;DR: we can accommodate an annual invoiced commitment with a multi-year discount, structured milepost credits for ramp, and quarterly true-ups (or monthly if needed) — details below.

Quick proposal (draft):
- Term: 12 or 24 months (we can price both).
- Commitment: we can structure an annual invoice for the committed token/embedding units.
- Pricing: baseline: list price; 12-month prepay: 8% discount; 24-month prepay: 12% discount.
- Ramp / milepost credits: for year-1 growth, offer credits that release at 3- and 6-month milestones to offset early over-commits while you scale. Example: 10% credit on invoiced amount at M3 and 5% at M6 (applied as account credit).
- True-ups: default quarterly true-up (aligns with finance cycles); monthly true-up available as an add-on.
- Termination/Fallback: standard pro-rata refund on unused prepay less a 60-day notice admin fee.

I've attached a short term sheet (ACME-Redwood-Terms-Initial.xlsx) that shows a worked example using your $480k starting point. Marissa (copied) is our AE and will pick up pricing/terms; we can bring Karthik from legal if you want redline-ready language.

Next steps: if the numbers look reasonable, we can send a contract draft and SOW for services; otherwise tell us which levers to move (higher discount vs. looser true-up cadence vs. larger upfront credit).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Director | Redwood Inference
From: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@acmehealth.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.io
Date: 2026-10-12T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching ACME billing to annual invoice - initial ask

Diego — this is helpful, thanks. A few clarifications from procurement/finance: 
- We prefer annual invoicing with a single payment per year tied to the committed amount (not monthly chargebacks).
- Can you move the M3 credit to be weighted earlier (e.g., 12% at M2 and 3% at M5) if we agree to a 24-month term? We need stronger early-year protection given our onboarding schedule.
- The quarterly true-up should be fine; procurement would accept monthly only if there is an automated billing connector — otherwise it creates manual reconciliation overhead.

One important constraint: our procurement team requires contract language that preserves a limited ramp protection — i.e., credits should not be refundable cash but account credit only, and credits must be applied before any price adjustments. Also SOC 2 appendix is required in contract.

I'll share the internal expected cadence: production rollout for two teams starting Jan 2027, larger batch in Apr 2027. That aligns with an early milepost being more valuable.

If you can send a 24-month worked example with the adjusted milepost weighting and the draft SOW we can route it through procurement this week.

—Emma
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching ACME billing to annual invoice - initial ask

Looping in Marissa (AE) and Laura (Finance) to lock on invoicing mechanics, and Karthik for redline support. Per Emma's ask, proposed adjustments below: 

Revised worked example (24-month term):
- Effective committed ARR (year-1 billable): $480,000 (annual invoice).
- Discount: 24-month prepay now priced at 13% (we can flex to 14% with a 10% larger commit).
- Milepost credits (account credit only): 12% of the year-1 invoice applied at month 2, 4% applied at month 5 (total 16%). Credits apply to future invoices and do not convert to cash.
- True-up: quarterly by default; offer automated billing connector integration for monthly true-ups (reduces reconciliation overhead).
- SOC 2: will include standard SOC 2 appendix; Laura, please attach the SOC 2 cert and data residency clause to the SOW.

Attachments: a draft SOW (ACME-SOW-Draft.pdf) and the updated term worksheet (updated tab in the attached XLSX).

Requesting Marissa to confirm final discount level and whether ACME will agree to account-credit-only for milepost concessions — once confirmed we'll generate a DocuSign-ready MSA + SOW and provide the HubSpot record and DocuSign link.

Marissa/Laura/Karthik — any objections to the revised numbers?

Thanks,
Diego

Onward.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@acmehealth.io>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching ACME billing to annual invoice - initial ask

Emma — thanks, we can do the 24-month at 13% with the milepost structure Diego suggested (12% at M2, 4% at M5) as account credits. We've uploaded the draft MSA + SOW to DocuSign and included the SOC 2 appendix and data residency language per your note.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/signature-request/ABCDEF123456
HubSpot opportunity: HS-87654321

I attached the two files referenced earlier to this thread. Please let us know if procurement needs any alternate payment terms (e.g., net-45 vs net-30) and we'll include that in the DocuSign envelope.

Looking forward to crossing the finish line — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps accelerate review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
